clips.send: Film studios (Fayetteville). Sound stages south of Atlanta. In 2008 Georgia began offering film and TV companies a tax credit of up to 30 percent of what they spend in the state. Big studio campuses grew up around Atlanta, such as Trilith Studios in Fayetteville and Tyler Perry Studios on the old Fort McPherson army base. Direct spending hit a record of about $4.4 billion in fiscal 2022, then fell to $2.6 billion in fiscal 2024 after Hollywood strikes.

clips.send: Port of Brunswick. America’s busiest port for autos and heavy machinery. Ships here are “roll-on/roll-off”: cars, tractors and bulldozers drive on and off. In 2024 and again in 2025 the Georgia Ports Authority reported Brunswick as the nation’s busiest port for autos and heavy equipment. 2025: about 779,000 autos plus more than 53,000 units of heavy machinery.

clips.send: Downtown Atlanta. Where the 1996 Games and two mayors reshaped a city. Maynard Jackson (mayor from 1974) and Andrew Young (1982–1990) helped turn Atlanta into an international city. Centennial Olympic Park, built for 1996 on run-down land, is now ringed by attractions such as the Georgia Aquarium, the World of Coca-Cola and the National Center for Civil and Human Rights — tourism in action. The Carter Center (founded by Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter in 1982) is a few miles east.

He died at home in Plains on December 29, 2024, aged 100 — the longest-lived US president. Jimmy Carter National Historical Park preserves his boyhood farm, school and campaign depot.

clips.send: Hartsfield-Jackson Airport. A gateway that puts most Americans within a short flight. William Hartsfield started the airport on an old racetrack in 1925. It has been the world’s busiest passenger airport since 1998 (73.5 million travelers that year) — except in 2020, when a Chinese airport passed it during COVID-19. Record: about 110.5 million passengers in 2019; 108.1 million in 2024. Five runways; a 400-foot control tower (2006).

clips.send: Port of Savannah. Georgia’s doorway to world trade. Garden City Terminal handles containers — standard steel boxes measured in TEU (one 20-foot box equals 1 TEU). The channel was deepened from 42 to 47 feet (2015–2022) so bigger ships can come in more fully loaded. Fiscal 2021: 5.3 million TEU — the first Southeast or Gulf port over 5 million. Record: 5.76 million in fiscal 2022.

clips.send: 布伦瑞克港。美国最繁忙的汽车和重型机械港口。这里的船是“滚装船”：汽车、拖拉机和推土机直接开上开下。 佐治亚港务局报告说，2024 年和 2025 年布伦瑞克都是美国最繁忙的汽车和重型机械港口。 2025 年：约 77.9 万辆汽车，另有 5.3 万多台重型机械。

clips.send: 萨凡纳港。佐治亚通往世界贸易的大门。加登城码头装卸集装箱——一种标准钢箱，用“标准箱，T E U，”计量（一个 20 英尺箱 等于 1 TEU）。 2015—2022 年，航道从 42 英尺挖深到 47 英尺，更大的船能装得更满进港。 2021 财年 530 万标准箱，是美国东南部和墨西哥湾沿岸第一个超过 500 万的港口；最高纪录是 2022 财年的 576 万。

clips.send: 哈茨菲尔德-杰克逊机场。让大多数美国人只需短途飞行就能到达的门户。1925 年，威廉·哈茨菲尔德在一座旧赛车场上建起了这座机场。 自 1998 年（当年旅客 7350 万人次）以来，它一直是世界上旅客最多的机场——只有 2020 年新冠疫情期间被中国的一座机场超过。 最高纪录：2019 年约 1.105 亿人次；2024 年 1.081 亿人次。有五条跑道，以及 2006 年建成的 400 英尺高的塔台。
